standard_basis.contract: R1 after ~1-2 subsequent learning items; R2 after ~4-6; R3 after ~10-14; intervals are heuristics but labels represent expanding review opportunities rather than arbitrary representations.

findings.adjudication: The sequence-5/6 R3 labels are premature under the repository's expanding-interval contract, and sequence 7 correctly behaves as an R2-distance opportunity. Unlike the quand case, no natural venir occurrence exists in the checked +10-to-14 passage window, so merely relabeling metadata would expose a missing R3 opportunity rather than fully repair the schedule.
findings.proposed_correction: Relabel the premature sequence-5/6 events to R2 (or otherwise normalize them consistently with the spacing contract), preserve sequence 7 as R2, and add a genuine later R3 retrieval/re-exposure opportunity only through a pedagogically natural canonical passage/task. Do not fabricate a metadata-only R3 event where venir is absent.

findings.adjudication: The sequence-6 R3 label is premature and causes the reported R3-to-R2 regression at sequence 8. A genuine later R3 opportunity already exists at sequence 11, close to the intended expanding interval. This is therefore a metadata-stage defect, not a missing-review defect.
findings.proposed_correction: Relabel the premature sequence-6 event as R2 while retaining sequence 11 as R3; rerun chronology and linkage checks after the edit.
